artDirection: Active title: research-based classic Pokemon title composition with the selected two-line logo, dynamic official FRLG cover illustrations, and a softly filtered energy texture animated with dual waves and moving gradient lighting. Fire renders warm red/orange with original FireRed title flame rows; leaf renders teal/lime with 44 original FRLG leaf sprite instances in back/front layers. Interior screens retain the approved GameCube-inspired low-poly lab backgrounds.
provenanceNote: The active title-energy texture is an OpenAI built-in imagegen reconstruction based on an actual Pokemon Box title screenshot, not an original Pokemon Box asset. Its installed violet/pink PNG is unchanged; WebGL supplies dual-sample wave motion, theme recoloring, and lighting. Active Charizard/Venusaur illustrations are official FRLG cover artwork downloaded unchanged from press-kit-sourced Bulbagarden files. The selected logo is copied unchanged; its sheen is a separate masked UI layer. Interior backgrounds remain generated layout-reference reconstructions. UI, characters, logo, and cover art are separate assets.

title.method: OpenAI built-in imagegen reference-based texture reconstruction, copied unchanged; renderer supplies dual-sample waves, fire/leaf recoloring, and gradient lighting
title.themeSelection: Selected once per opening, retained when returning to title. Successive openings alternate when localStorage is available; the initial choice uses a random seed.
title.note: Generated texture contains no logo, characters, controls, or text. These are independent layers. Original FireRed title flames are active in overlapping rows; the original battle-flame sheet and earlier title raster/procedural experiments remain inactive.
title.effectScaling: Linear texture filtering on a full-screen WebGL quad with aspect-preserving cover crop and two animated texture samples; up to 30 rendered frames per second

effects.fire: Warm red/orange shader recoloring, dual texture waves, moving gradient illumination, and overlapping rising rows from the original FireRed title flame frames
effects.leaf: Teal/lime shader recoloring preserving whites; 44 original FRLG leaf sprite instances split into 24 back and 20 foreground instances with drift, rotation, and foreground shadows
effects.reducedMotion: Static backdrop and sprite composition; a stationary subset of leaves; logo sheen disabled
effects.fallback: Animated Canvas 2D fallback uses a 640 x 360 intermediate canvas, two warped texture passes, theme recoloring, and moving gradient lighting; independent sprite layers remain available
effects.depth: Mascot illustration shadows and separate foreground/background sprite canvases
effects.logoSheen: Separate white CSS gradient masked to the unchanged logo PNG; 5.4-second cycle
effects.provenance: Reference-based generated reconstruction; no original Pokemon Box background texture or animation code is used

title.sourceTextureColors: Original installed PNG remains violet, cobalt, and pink; warm fire and teal/lime variants are runtime color transformations.

main.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset: one full-bleed 16:9 PRE-RENDERED GAMECUBE-ERA VIDEOGAME BACKGROUND. Art direction mandatory: look like an actual 2003-2005 Nintendo GameCube Pokémon Colosseum or XD environment render. Low polygon geometry with clear broad faces, modest smooth shading on simple models, flat/simple low-resolution baked diffuse textures, broad clean color areas, subdued vertex lighting, basic soft shadow blobs, simple plastic materials. This must look like a 2004 console game screenshot at 640x360 resolution enlarged cleanly, with limited early-2000s polygon budgets. NO modern cinematic realism, NO physically based materials, NO granular surface microdetail, NO photoreal texture, NO painterly brushwork, NO ray tracing, NO glossy raytraced reflections, NO depth of field, NO blur, NO film grain. Every surface simple and graphic. Reference image is COMPOSITION ONLY, change the rendering style completely to early GameCube. NO text, NO logos, NO UI, NO menu, NO border or bars. Preserve reference's main layout but simplify entire room: modern professor laboratory with large rectangular blue windows, plain gray concrete pillars, blocky bookcase and simple map. Beige box-shaped desktop CRT and simple keyboard on left third of blue-gray counter, blue monitor with simple white pokeball symbol. Two small red-white pokeballs. Countertop is solid smooth blue-gray with faint fake baked reflection, no marble texture. Reserve space immediately right of PC for independently layered Pikachu. Right half quiet dim wall/books for menu. No characters in this background.

coastalTitle.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create one clean pre-rendered Nintendo GameCube-era title-screen BACKGROUND environment, circa 2003-2005 console graphics. Full 16:9. Scene: sunset over ocean seen from cliff, simple angular broad-faced rock ledges in left and right lower foreground are EMPTY and wide enough for separately rendered characters. A simple white lighthouse with dark pointed roof on far upper-left hill, small coastal town of simple colored cube houses below left, rock stacks out in ocean right, low orange sun around 65% across horizon, broad pink-orange gradient sky filling upper half. Art direction must be original Pokémon Colosseum/XD kind of low polygon 3D world: simple broad geometry, flat low-resolution diffuse textures, basic vertex lighting, simple shadow blobs, ocean as flat plane with a few broad repeating painted highlights. Clear nostalgic 2004 console image. NOT modern realistic graphics, NOT painterly illustration. No microtexture, no granular stones, no photographic waves, no realism, no modern ray traced reflections, no depth of field, no film grain. NO characters or creatures, I will composite separate character assets later. NO words, NO logo, NO UI. Clean simple colorful game environment.
coastalTitle.note: Earlier coastal title raster retained on disk as an inactive reference. It is not used by the active title card.

screenTransitions.swapBehavior: Wait for the synchronous or asynchronous screen-swap callback while fully covered, then two render frames before revealing. The launcher render promise includes title-effect readiness and rendered image decoding.
screenTransitions.reducedMotion: No fade animation; swap and cleanup still run
screenTransitions.lifecycle: Reject overlapping transitions, block pointer input during transitions, and clear overlay/input blocking after completion, cancellation, disposal, or errors
screenTransitions.nativeReturnReset: The launcher-game-return event and status-poll exit path call the shared return routine. It clears pending launch/navigation/controller repeat state, invalidates older asynchronous generations, and calls the transition reset to cancel animation, resolve pending render-frame waits, and remove overlay input blocking.

nativeGameReturn.nativeBehavior: ShowLauncher hides the game panel, shows and focuses WebView, then explicitly dispatches the browser event and focuses WebView again if no new game has started.
nativeGameReturn.browserBehavior: Shared restore routine clears pending, launchingGame, navigationPending, lastPadAction, and lastPadTime; increments navigation/state/game generations; resets screen transitions; refreshes backend state and audio; preserves existing error/confirmation dialogs.
nativeGameReturn.pollingFallback: A running-to-idle backend status transition invokes the same restore routine.
